headline: GOLD RALLY ON THIN ICE — Natixis Warns $3,340 Downside Scenario Still Alive Despite Monday's 4% Bounce
snippet: Natixis analyst Bernard Dahdah cautioned on November 23 that gold's 4% recovery from 15-month lows is likely to be short-lived, with a downside scenario targeting $3,340 per ounce if the December Fed meeting delivers a hawkish surprise. The warning arrives the same day gold bounced above $3,600, with Dahdah noting the structural drivers of the correction — a US dollar at 19-month highs and near-certainty pricing for a December rate hike — remain intact. For retail investors attempting to call a bottom in junior gold equities, the Natixis bear case provides critical context: a failed bounce at current levels would put gold back below the break-even costs of many marginal producers.

headline: ENERGY FUELS SURGES 8% ON PLAN TO PROCESS 1 MILLION POUNDS OF URANIUM IN DECEMBER — Oklo +12%, NuScale +13% Join Nuclear Equity Rally
snippet: Energy Fuels (NYSE: UUUU) jumped 8% on November 23 after announcing the restart of its White Mesa Mill uranium processing campaign in December 2026, targeting approximately one million pounds of uranium concentrate through Q1 2027. The announcement added a production-side catalyst to the sentiment-driven uranium equity rally already underway on Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia — with Oklo climbing 12% and NuScale Power gaining 13% as AI datacenter demand optimism was partially restored.

headline: GOLD FELL $500 IN 8 SESSIONS TO 15-MONTH LOWS — APMEX: Thanksgiving Week's PCE Print Is Now the Year's Most Important Gold Catalyst
snippet: APMEX's market commentary documents that gold lost approximately $500 per ounce across just eight trading sessions — the fastest dollar-decline since 2020 — driven by margin calls from the AI tech selloff and aggressive repricing of Fed rate hike expectations. The piece frames Wednesday's PCE inflation data as the pivotal test: a hot print revives near-certainty of a December 50bps hike and could send gold back below $3,500, while an in-line or soft reading could allow Monday's bounce to consolidate. Thin Thanksgiving-week liquidity amplifies the stakes of either outcome.

headline: PCE REPORT WEDNESDAY IS GOLD'S MAKE-OR-BREAK MOMENT — Thanksgiving Thin Liquidity Could Amplify Any Inflation Surprise
snippet: Gold and silver's Monday rebound faces its first real test Wednesday when the Fed's preferred PCE inflation gauge lands before US markets close for Thanksgiving Thursday. Analysts warn that a hotter-than-expected print would revive near-certain pricing for a December rate hike and could send gold back toward $3,450–$3,500, potentially erasing the entire recovery in one session. Volume is running roughly 40% below normal through the holiday weekend, meaning any forced liquidation would have outsized price impact in thin conditions — making this one of the year's highest-stakes macro prints for precious metals investors.

headline: MINING ETFs ERASED 16–19% IN ONE WEEK — Weekly Ore Report: One Critical Signal Still Missing Before Calling a Floor
snippet: SilverGoldAlpha's weekly newsletter documents that junior mining ETFs lost between 16% and 19% in the week ending November 23 — the worst single-week destruction of equity value since 2020 — and identifies the specific technical signal that has historically confirmed genuine capitulation bottoms but is not yet present in current data. The analysis is essential reading for anyone weighing GDXJ or individual junior miner entries: distinguishing a real capitulation flush from a continuation of a primary downtrend is the difference between catching a floor and averaging into a deteriorating position in one of the worst environments of the decade.

headline: COT DATA FLASHING BULLISH PRECIOUS METALS SETUP — Kitco Analysis: Patience, Not Urgency, Is the Correct Response
snippet: A Kitco opinion piece published November 23 analyzes Commitments of Traders data showing managed money net positioning in gold and silver approaching extreme bearish levels — a configuration that has historically preceded major recoveries. The author's key distinction: the same COT conditions have occasionally marked the beginning of extended downtrends rather than bottoms, and Wednesday's PCE data is a critical filter. The piece argues for building a watchlist and defining entry criteria rather than buying the bounce.

headline: NRC OPENS COMMENT PERIOD ON CROWNPOINT URANIUM ISR PROJECT — New Mexico DOJ Wins Right to Intervene in Controversial Mine Renewal
snippet: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission opened a public comment period on November 23 on its draft environmental assessment for NuFuels' Crownpoint in-situ recovery uranium project in New Mexico's McKinley County — the same day the NRC granted the New Mexico Department of Justice's petition to intervene in the license renewal proceeding. The Crownpoint ISR project has faced tribal and state opposition for decades, and the granted DOJ intervention means New Mexico can formally contest NuFuels' application on environmental grounds. The case sets a precedent for how aggressively state attorneys general can challenge federal uranium licensing decisions across the western US.

headline: FREEPORT-McMoRAN FLASHES RARE BEAR SIGNAL DESPITE COPPER BOUNCE — Historical Pattern Bullish Only 20% of the Time One Month Later
snippet: Schaeffer's Investment Research flagged Freeport-McMoRan (NYSE: FCX) as triggering a specific technical bear signal on November 23 — the same day copper bounced from its bear market lows. Historical backtesting shows the stock was higher one month later only 20% of the time following this signal. For junior copper explorers whose valuations track FCX, the warning adds weight to the thesis that Monday's bounce is a technical relief rally in a primary downtrend, not the start of a sustained recovery.

headline: SUMITOMO COMMITS A$58.8M TO ARDEA'S GOONGARRIE NICKEL-COBALT PRE-FEED — WA's 250,000-Tonne Cobalt Resource Advances Toward Feasibility
snippet: Japan's Sumitomo Metal Mining and Mitsubishi, through their joint venture GH Nickel, committed A$58.8 million on November 23 to fund pre-FEED engineering work at Ardea Resources' Goongarrie Hub in Western Australia — one of the world's largest undeveloped nickel-cobalt resources at approximately 250,000 tonnes of contained cobalt. The Japanese consortium funded the full pre-feasibility engineering tranche, an unusual show of conviction in a nickel market where Australian mines are curtailing and closing. The move suggests strategic battery-critical minerals motivation as Japan accelerates efforts to secure supply outside Chinese influence.

headline: CHILE'S $111 BILLION MINING PIPELINE RESTS ON TWO UNAPPROVED LITHIUM PERMITS — Atacama Environmental Bottleneck Threatens Record Investment Target
snippet: Chile's state copper commission Cochilco reported the country's mining investment pipeline has reached $111.1 billion — the largest portfolio in 13 years — but virtually all of the growth above copper's baseline comes from two lithium projects sharing a single salt flat, neither of which has environmental approval. Both face Indigenous community opposition and water scarcity objections in the Atacama. For lithium investors tracking supply-side risk, Chile's headline investment figure is built on regulatory outcomes that remain deeply uncertain.
